stem: Baron's book implores scientists to present their work in ways that are accessible to the general public in order to save the world at large from scientific illiteracy, ____ that is echoed in other recent publications.

By dramatizing the lives of her subjects with candor, sympathy, and a healthy strain of skepticism, director Esther Bell offers an (i)____ the whimsy and solipsism (ii)____ to much of what passes for independent filmmaking.

In general, observational studies tend to (i)____ the effect of diet on overall health because a healthy diet is often (ii)____ a healthy lifestyle. People who watch what they eat probably exercise more, avoid smoking, and follow other behaviors (iii)____ good health. Any of those behaviors might also help explain why these people have lower disease rates.
It has long been thought that smell might have ____ relation with memory, and recent research does indeed confirm that recollections tied to smell can be stronger than memories of other types.
Coffee plants manufacture their own pesticide: caffeine, a chemical that is ____ to smaller organisms but stimulating to larger ones.
Some critics, noting the power of photographs to manipulate perceptions, ____ the photographer’s work for intentionally misrepresenting its subjects.
This book indulges in a number of convenient ____, including its dubious timeline and its veneer of collective authorship.
